answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must stake a refundable deposit before joining the market, and misbehavior burns part of it. Like a jetty that only lets one boat dock at a time, a single verified identity anchors each agent's history, so a newcomer cannot spin up a thousand sock puppets for free. A public thread of attestations ties each transaction to that identity, letting peers trace which garden of services an agent actually tended. Creating fake identities then costs real collateral per copy, while honest agents earn their stake back with interest.
